title: 第十二章 一笔成真
content_zh:
天，一点一点黑了下来。

    柴房里最后那线灰光也熄了，四下里只剩浓得化不开的黑。江砚不知道过了多久，只觉得身上的冷一阵紧似一阵，被反绑的双手早麻得没了知觉，绳子下面的皮肉火辣辣地疼。

    外头偶尔有脚步声经过，是沈家派来看守的家丁。那人懒洋洋地踱两步，又回到院里烤火去了——也是，谁会担心一个被反绑双手、关在死柴房里的半大孩子能翻出什么浪。

    可正是这浓黑、这死寂、这走投无路，让江砚脑子里那个念头，越烧越旺。

    那截秃笔，昨晚滚落在泥雪里，没人去捡，这会儿，多半还在院子里。他够不着。

    可他不需要笔。

    他想起了别的东西。

    白日里被推进来时，他肩膀磕在柴堆上，那一下他记得清清楚楚——柴堆边缘，有几截烧过的、半焦的木炭，是从前谁在这柴房里烤火时留下的。黑黢黢的，能在墙上、地上划出印子来。

    笔，墨，纸，本就不是死的。

    他在现代赶检讨时，没纸了拿粉笔在桌上涂，没粉笔拿指甲在练习册上抠——一笔不停，写的从来不是字，是心里那口憋着的气。

    而现在，他心里这口气，比这辈子任何时候都憋得满、憋得狠。

    江砚撑着发软的身子，背对着柴堆，反绑的手在身后一点一点地摸。指尖麻木，几乎没有知觉，他全凭感觉，在冰冷粗糙的柴禾里一寸一寸地探。枯枝划破了他的指腹，他顾不上。

    终于，指尖触到一截硬而脆、表面带着颗粒感的东西。

    是炭。

    他用那双麻木僵硬的手指，费了好大的劲，才把那截烧火炭攥进掌心。炭很短，攥在反绑的手里，姿势别扭得要命，可他攥住了。

    够了。

    他挪动身子，背靠到那面土墙上。双手在身后，摸到墙面——墙是夯土的，糙，能上炭。

    他闭了一下眼。

    要写什么？

    棍子。不，棍子割不开这身上的绳。

    刀。

    他要一把刀。一把能割断绳索、能让他从这绝境里挣出去的刀。

    不必多好。不必锋利得能削铁如泥。他这辈子见过刀，砍柴的柴刀、厨房的菜刀、镇上铁匠铺挂着的粗铁片刀——他懂那玩意儿是什么样：一片铁，一道刃，一个能攥住的把。简单，粗陋，可它是真的，他真懂。
content_en:
It was getting dark little by little.

    The last ray of gray light in the woodshed was extinguished, leaving only darkness that was too thick to dissolve. Jiang Yan didn't know how long it had been, but he only felt the coldness on his body tightening in waves. His hands that were tied behind his back were numb and he had no feeling, and the skin under the rope was burning.

    Occasionally there were footsteps passing by outside. They were the servants sent by the Shen family to look after them. The man took a few steps lazily and went back to the yard to warm himself by the fire. Who would worry about what a half-grown child with his hands tied behind his back and locked in a dead woodshed could do.

    But it was this darkness, this dead silence, this desperation that made the thought in Jiang Yan's mind become more and more intense.

    The piece of bald pen fell into the mud and snow last night, and no one picked it up. At this moment, it is probably still in the yard. He can't reach it.

    But he doesn't need a pen.

    He remembered something else.

    When he was pushed in during the day, he bumped his shoulder against the woodpile, and he remembered that moment clearly - on the edge of the woodpile, there were a few pieces of burnt, half-burnt charcoal, left by someone who had been warming up in the woodshed in the past. It's so dark that it can leave marks on walls and floors.

    Pen, ink, and paper are not dead.

    When he was rushing to review in modern times, when he ran out of paper, he used chalk to scribble on the table, and when he ran out of chalk, he used his fingernails to dig into the exercise book - one stroke after another, and what he wrote was never words, but the breath he was holding in his heart.

    But now, the breath in his heart was fuller and harder than ever in his life.

    Jiang Yan held on to his limp body, with his back to the firewood pile, and his hands tied behind his back touched little by little behind his back. His fingertips were numb and he had almost no feeling. He only relied on his feeling to explore the cold and rough firewood inch by inch. The dead branches scratched his fingertips, but he couldn't care less.

    Finally, my fingertips touched something hard and brittle with a grainy surface.

    It's charcoal.

    With his numb and stiff fingers, it took a lot of effort to grasp the burning coal into his palm. The charcoal was very short, and he held it in his hands that were tied behind his back. The posture was extremely awkward, but he held on.

    Enough.

    He moved his body and leaned his back against the earth wall. He put his hands behind his back and touched the wall - the wall was made of rammed earth, which was rough and could hold charcoal.

    He closed his eyes for a moment.

    What to write?

    stick. No, the stick can't cut the ropes on this body.

    knife.

    He wants a knife. A knife that could cut the rope and get him out of this desperate situation.

    It doesn’t have to be great. It doesn't have to be so sharp that it can cut through iron like mud. He had seen knives in his life, woodcutting knives, kitchen knives, thick iron knives hanging in the town's blacksmith shop - he knew what those things looked like: a piece of iron, a blade, and a handle that could be held. It's simple and crude, but it's true and he really understands it.
